# Largest 3-Same-Digit Number in String. A found triple is written as its
# three characters ("000", never "0"); no triple is the empty string "".

@example The triples are 111, 888 and 222; the one of the highest digit is 888.
"51118882220"
=> "888"

@example The only triple is three zeros, returned as they stand.
"98000"
=> "000"

@example 5 occurs four times and 4 three times, but never three adjacent copies of one digit.
"5545544"
=> ""

# The shortest input: the whole string is the only window.
"999"
=> "999"

"000"
=> "000"

# The same digit at both ends of a window, a different one in the middle.
"303"
=> ""

# 9 occurs five times, in pairs and alone, never three adjacent.
"9989899"
=> ""

# Pairs of 9 don't count; the triple of 8 does.
"99899888"
=> "888"

# A triple at the very start.
"777123"
=> "777"

# A triple in the last window only.
"12345666"
=> "666"

# The larger triple comes second, then first.
"111999"
=> "999"

"9990111"
=> "999"

# Zeros first, a higher triple later.
"0001222"
=> "222"

# 1000 copies of one digit: still a single triple.
""
=> "333"

# 1000 digits in pairs, with no triple anywhere.
""
=> ""

# Random cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"00999999999"
=> "999"

@gen 2 small
"190001100"
=> "000"

@gen 3 small
"11111112"
=> "111"

@gen 4 small
"211111"
=> "111"

@gen 5 small
"555555500555"
=> "555"

@gen 6 small
"7788"
=> ""

@gen 7
""
=> "777"

@gen 8
""
=> "999"
